content:
SECTION 1  
* A 24-year-old says older people criticise young adults for spending any money on small pleasures like holidays or meals out, saying they should save everything for a house.  
* They argue that, with house prices high, few homes available, and banks not wanting to lend much, owning a home is probably impossible for many young people.  
* Because of this, they feel they’ll be stuck renting forever, paying lots of money to landlords who then accuse them of being financially irresponsible.  
* Another person points out that there are no real “special deals” or big discounts for under-25s; instead, what’s actually lower for them is their pay.  
* Young workers under 25 are legally allowed to be paid less than older adults for the same work, often earn very little even full-time, and are more likely to have insecure zero-hours contracts.
